Lena K.: quick heads-up: I prototyped an alternate approach to small-page grouping for offload. goal: keep compaction benefits without creating eviction hot spots for pinned micro-batches.

Omar T.: curious 97 what's the gist?

Lena K.: instead of a header byte, try a 'group descriptor' stored in the arena footer. descriptor contains: group_id, refcount, flags. small allocs inside the slab point to group_id with a 16-bit tag (packed into existing free-list word).

Jia W.: footer table sounds compact, but how do you handle cross-slab groups? we saw guest-kv sometimes spans contiguous allocs that cross slab boundaries during resizes.

Lena K.: good catch. we restrict group lifetime to within a slab (no cross-slab groups). when a guest cache region grows and spans slabs, we create a new group and link groups via a lightweight chain entry in the footer. eviction sees the chain and may evict chain members sequentially.

Ravi M.: performance? any microbench numbers vs header byte and side-table?

Lena K.: ran a 100k-request microbatch scenario: footer-descriptor approach increases allocation path by ~3us median and p99 ~12us, but reduces RAM overhead to near-zero vs header. header-byte approach was ~0.5% RAM + 0us allocation overhead. side-table was +9us median CPU.

Omar T.: so footer wins memory but costs latency. our SLAs prefer latency. doesn't look great.

Jia W.: could we hybridize: use header token for hot arenas (low-allocation-cost fast path) and footer descriptors for cold arenas (to save RAM)? the allocator could promote/demote slabs based on allocation rate.

Ravi M.: that could work. promotion policy: when slab allocation rate > X alloc/sec set header mode. when below threshold for Y seconds, flip to footer mode and compact. need background job to migrate descriptors -> header bits and vice versa.

Lena K.: migration cost is the tricky part. moving from footer->header requires walking slab and patching each allocation header; that's heavy. but we can do background incremental migration during low load windows and use epoch gating so we avoid races with pin/unpin.

Omar T.: what about eviction semantics: header bit allowed whole-group fast-evict. footer chain gives us sequential evict of members 97 that might be slower but more granular. Which behavior do we want for tenant fairness?

Jia W.: for fairness, granular is better. whole-group evict can starve other tenants if group is large. But for fragmentation reduction, whole-group evict helps keep compactness. Recommend making eviction policy pluggable per-tenant: tenant can pick aggressive compaction (favor whole-group) vs fair-evict (favor per-page). default: fair-evict.

Ravi M.: add telemetry: per-tenant compaction mode, eviction counts, tail latency when group evicts. we need dashboards before flipping defaults.

Lena K.: agreed. concrete action items: (1) add slab-footer group descriptor prototype (2) implement promote/demote hybrid rules (3) make eviction policy tenant-configurable with telemetry labels (4) build migration worker with epoch gating and incremental op limits. I'll open an RFC + perf appendix.

infra-bot: CI: staging/allocator-experiments #718 passed 97 perf-run attached: https://ci.internal/staging/718

Omar T.: please include the allocation-rate thresholds and migration budget assumptions in the RFC.

Jia W.: also include a failure model: what if migration aborts mid-slab? ensure pins keep working and any partial migration is rollback-safe.

Lena K.: will do. planning to test in canary tomorrow. tagging @Ravi M. for telemetry design review.

Ravi M.: noted. will sketch dashboard queries and a couple of alert rules.

Lena K.: thanks. I'll post the RFC link here when ready.
